chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Basir said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married off his female slave to a free man or to the slave of another group. He said: He does not have the right to take her back. If he sold her, and the buyer wished to take her from the man, he may do so.

key_terms.الَّذِي اشْتَرَاهَا: the one who bought her (the buyer)
key_terms.يَنزِعَهَا: to take her back / revoke the marriage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a master's right to annul his female slave's marriage if she is sold?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the legal mechanism of *tabi' al-talaq* (consequential divorce) in Shia jurisprudence, where the sale of a married slave woman effectively dissolves her marriage to her current husband. It highlights the master's retained right of revocation (*ruju'*) only through the act of sale, distinguishing this from a formal judicial divorce. This ruling underscores the fluidity of marital status in the context of slavery, where ownership transfer directly impacts the marital bond.
